cards.note: Very common Arizona bollard. No surrounding states use it
Very common bollard in California and many unique variations. When there are three letters it's the abbreviation of the county

Green flat bollards are very common and unique to Colorado. They come with 1-3 white or yellow (red is rare) reflector squares. Colorado also uses the same reflector circles as New Mexico but the green "stem" is much more common in Colorado.
Mostly found in West Virginia, Mississippi and Texas.

Diamond Reflectors are used by many states but most notably Montana and South Dakota. North Dakota and Minnesota only use them on highways. If you see them in the east you're probably in Connecticut or New York

This flat guardrail square is used a lot in Virginia, Maryland, Ohio, and Florida. Also found in Wisconsin, Minnesota, Nebraska, North and South Dakota but these states don't use a lot of guardrails so they will be rarer there.
These are very common in Idaho and Utah, when the white reflector is all the way to the top it's often Utah, and when it's not all the way to the top it's often Idaho
Like half of the time, Maine uses these tall flat bollards instead of the red/green rectangles on guardrails
You'll find these before and after guardrails. Unique to Minnesota
Missouri uses these small rounded reflectors, it's the only place I've seen them

In Nebraska, you'll find a lot of the black Wyoming bollards with a big reflector, rounded orange rectangles and small white circle reflectors. A combination of any of them should be confirmation of Nebraska
This is one is unique to Nevada and very common
New Mexico uses a white circle reflector in turns and three stacked orange circles (with a single orange circle on its back) before/after a turn. Not unique, used a lot in Colorado
Few things here, the tall sticks with white and green rounded rectangles or small squares or a single diamond. This specific guardrail is also very common in NY.

cards.a: Nothing Worth Remembering / Only On Highways
cards.note: These states don't use anything useful or only use stuff on highways. Some of these states have useful guardrail bollard metas, but that's covered in different locations
Unique for Oregon and very common. The grey part at the top is what's unique
Pennsylvania uses a lot of these flat white ones with a big grey reflector that's smaller at the bottom, often with a black cap. Many states use this default looking bollard on their highways only.
Massachusetts, New Hampshire, and Maine use these on guardrails. Red at the start and green at the end. Sometimes Maine uses tall flat bollards with the same colors instead.
These can pop up everywhere but New Mexico, Colorado, Nebraska and Wyoming use them a lot

Texas is recognizable by the unique guardrail bollard with an "inflated" bottom part. Sometimes they're just flat and not unique. Texas uses a lot of reflector tape on signs and mailboxes. The flat white bollard with three orange squares is unique to Texas
Blue diamond at the start and green diamond at the end of guardrails
The flat brown one is unique and very common, the flat white one is not unique but very common
These are mostly found in Michigan, New Hampshire and Rhode Island. Michigan's are longer/taller
These black on white bollards are unique to Wisconsin and used a lot

Wyoming has unique black bollards with 1-3 white or orange reflector squares. There's one version with one big reflector which is also used a lot in Nebraska. Then there's the white circle reflector with a painted top of the pole which is unique to Wyoming
